title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Desk Guide: Provisional Ceiling on the Allowance after a Disallowance
content:
For a dependency disallowance on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, the redetermined allowance is capped according to the age of the latest monetary determination on the claim: the number of calendar days from the latest monetary determination date to the handling date. The weekly benefit amount against which the ceiling is set is the one on the claim.

| Age of the latest monetary determination | Ceiling on the redetermined allowance |
|---|---|
| No more than 21 days (the redetermination window) | 0.04 (4 percent) of the weekly benefit amount, rounded to the cent |
| More than 21 days but no more than 90 days | 0.06 (6 percent) of the weekly benefit amount, rounded to the cent |
| More than 90 days | No ceiling |

The ceiling applies to the redetermined allowance before it is subtracted from the allowance on the claim; the redetermined allowance is the lesser of the figure computed for the dependents counted and the ceiling.

## Boundary days

| Determination age | Ceiling |
|---|---|
| 21 days | 4 percent |
| 22 days | 6 percent |
| 90 days | 6 percent |
| 91 days | None |

### Hypothetical figures

For a weekly benefit amount of 346.00 the 4 percent ceiling is 13.84 and the 6 percent ceiling is 20.76. On a determination 10 days old, a computed allowance of 30.00 is capped at 13.84, and against 45.00 on the claim the decrease is 31.16.
